sn22.83:1.2: There the Venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn22.83:2.1: “Friends, the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantaniputta was very helpful to us when we were newly ordained.
sn22.83:2.2: He exhorted us with the following exhortation:
sn22.83:2.3: “It is by clinging, Ānanda, that the notion ‘I am’ occurs, not without clinging. And by clinging to what does ‘I am’ occur, not without clinging?
sn22.83:2.5: It is by clinging to form that ‘I am’ occurs, not without clinging.
sn22.83:2.6: It is by clinging to feeling …
sn22.83:2.9: to consciousness that ‘I am’ occurs, not without clinging.
sn22.83:3.1: “Suppose, friend Ānanda, a young woman—or a man—youthful and fond of ornaments, would examine her own facial image in a mirror or in a bowl filled with pure, clear, clean water: she would look at it with clinging, not without clinging.
sn22.83:3.2: So too, it is by clinging to form that ‘I am’ occurs, not without clinging.
sn22.83:3.3: It is by clinging to feeling …
sn22.83:3.6: to consciousness that ‘I am’ occurs, not without clinging.
sn22.83:4.11: He understands: ‘… there is no more for this state of being.’”
sn22.83:4.12: “Friends, the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantaniputta was very helpful to us when we were newly ordained.
sn22.83:4.13: He exhorted us with that exhortation.
sn22.83:4.14: And when I heard his Dhamma teaching I made the breakthrough to the Dhamma.”
